--- title: "Who Receives Technical Violations?" format: html --- **Who receives technical violations?** 1. What proportion of youth on probation supervision receive a technical violation during a probation term? How does this vary across race/ethnicity, sex, age, and risk level? 2. What proportion of violations filed by a PO are rejected by supervisor or prosecutor?

# 3. Supervisor/Prosecutor Rejections **Business Rule:** According to Dallas County, all of the technical violation records without a referral number indicate that a PO filed the violation, but that it was rejected by a supervisor. **NOTE:** Only about 2% of all violations fit this criteria -- not sure if it warrants analysis (especially anything disaggregated). The Dallas team mentioned several factors to consider regarding rejections in general as well as the small percentage of violations that appear in our sample. A fair amount of informal rejection is possible (possible violations are rejected/not approved before any data would be entered or a violation would actually be filed). PO has to get permission from supervisor before filing a violation so there should be very few rejected violations (i.e., PO's will likely only formally file a violation if they feel confident it will be approved by a supervisor).Thus, 2% really only reflects what is in the data system but likely does not speak to the real trend.
